senses: to run to help, to run to the aid of, hasten to assist
to run beneath, go under; to undergo
la:verb:succurro.html:
suc-curro (subc-), curri, cursum, 3, v. n.,
to run under.
Lit.
In gen.: tempore eodem aliud nequeat succurrere lunae Corpus, * ; cf.: pagus Succusanus, quod succurrit Carinis, runs, i. e. lies under or behind, Müll.—
In partic., to run or hasten to the aid or assistance of one; to help, aid, assist, succor (the predom. and class, signif.; syn.: subvenio, adjuvo, sublevo): ut laborantibus succurrat,: saluti fortunisque communibus,: succurrit illi Varenus et laboranti subvenit,: laborantibus,; : afflictis semper,: suis cedentibus auxilio,: domino,: oppido, Auct. B. Afr. 5, 1.—
Of things, to be useful for, good against: tantis malis,. — Esp., of medicines: cannabis succurrit alvo jumentorum,helps, relieves,: strangulationibus (crethmos),: venenis fungorum (nitrum),: dum succurrere humanis erroribus cupiunt, ipsi se in errores maximos induxerunt, .—Impers. pass.: se confidere munitionibus oppidi, si celeriter succurratur,; ; ; ; ; : paratae lites: succurrendum'st,.—
Trop. *
In gen.: licet undique omnes in me terrores periculaque impendeant omnia, succurram atque subibo,I will encounter and undergo them,.—
In partic., to come into the mind, occur to one (class.; esp. freq. after the Aug. period; syn. subit): ut quidque succurrit, libet scribere,: illud etiam mihi succurrebat, grave esse, etc., id. fil. ap. : alicui,; ; et saep.: succurrit versus ille Homericus, etc., Aug. ap. fin.—Impers.: non succurrit tibi, quamdiu circum Bactra haereas,: neque cuiquam facile succurrat,.—With inf.: et illud annotare succurrit, unum omnino, etc.,: mirari succurrit,; .

la:verb:succumbo.gloss: to sink, fall, lie or break down
senses: to sink, fall, lie or break down
to surrender, to yield, to succumb
la:verb:succumbo.html:
suc-cumbo (subc-), cŭbŭi, cŭbĭtum, 3, v. n.,
to lay or put one's self under any thing; to fall down, lie, or sink down.
Lit. (rare; not in Cic.; cf. subsido).
In gen.: ancipiti succumbens victima ferro,: vidit Cyllenius omnes Succubuisse oculos, had sunk in sleep, i. e. had closed, : (Augustus) Nolae succubuit,took to his bed,: non succumbentibus causis operis,; Hildebr.—
In partic.
Of a woman, to lie down to a man, to cohabit with him (cf. substerno): alicui,; ; ; ; ; ; .—
With dat., of a woman, to be a rival to: alumnae Tethyos,; .—
Trop., to yield, be overcome; to submit, surrender, succumb (the predom. and class. signif.; cf.: cedo, me summitto).
With dat. (so most freq.): philosopho succubuit orator,: qui Cannensi ruinae non succubuissent,: arrogantiae divitum,: cur succumbis cedisque fortunae?; ; cf.: nulli neque homini neque perturbationi animi nec fortunae,: magno animo et erecto est, nec umquam succumbet inimicis, ne fortunae quidem,: mihi,: labori, Caes. B. G, 7, 86: oneri,: doloribus,: senectuti,: crimini,: magis,; : culpae,; : tempori,to yield,: pugnae,: precibus,: voluntati alicujus,.—
Absol.: non esse viri debilitari dolore, frangi, succumbere,: huic (socero) subvenire volt succumbenti jam et oppresso,: succubuit famae victa puella metu,: hac ille perculsus plagā non succubuit,: succumbe, virtus,: labefacta mens succubuit,; . —*
With inf.: nec ipsam perpeti succubuisset,.

la:noun:successio.html:
successĭo, ōnis, f.
succedo, II.
.
A coming into the place of another, a following after, succeeding, succession in office, possession, etc. (mostly post-Aug.): si merces Antonii oppressi poscitur in Antonii locum successio, Brut. ap. : Neronis principis successio,: quorum non dubia,; ; ; : ad spem successionis admoveri,; : regni,; ; .—Plur.: magistratibus judicia per annuas successiones permisit,: familiae, quae per successiones jus sibi vindicant,: morbi per successiones quasdam traduntur,: jura successionum,: doloris amotio successionem afficit voluptatis,.—*
A good issue, success: successio prospera consecuta est, Aug. (perh. Cic. Hort. Fragm.) Vit. Beat. 26: victoriam proeliorum successionibus relaturos,.

la:verb:succedo.gloss: to climb, mount or ascend, go from under; go up
senses: to climb, mount or ascend, go from under; go up
to march on, advance, march up to, approach
to follow, succeed in, to relieve (with dative of the thing or person being succeeded)
to enter, go under, come under
la:verb:succedo.html:
suc-cēdo, cessi, cessum, 3, v. n. and a.
[sub].
To go below or under (so mostly poet.; syn. subeo).
Lit.
In gen., to enter, go under, come under: simul ac primum nubes succedere soli Coepere,to go under the sun,; cf. : tectum, cui imbris vitandi causā succederet,: maestae Succedunt ramis volucres,: succedere tectis,; so, tectis,; : rex jussae succedit aquae,: tecto et umbrae,: antro, and 19: tumulo sineret succedere terrae,i. e. to be buried,; cf.: serpens imo Successit tumulo,.—
In partic., to go from under; to go up, mount, ascend: alto caelo,to mount, ascend,: in arduum,; cf.: hoc itinere est fons, quo mare succedit longius,: muros,; ; ; : tumulum, et saep. — Absol.: erigi scalas jussit ac promptissimum quemque succedere,.—Poet.: in montem succedere silvas Cogebant,to retreat to the mountains,.—
Trop.
To come under, submit to any thing: omnes sententiae verbaque omnia ... sub acumen stili subeant et succedant necesse est,: externae dominationi, quam in suis timuerunt, sponte succedunt,: succedoque oneri,take up,: nec qui succederet operi inventus est,undertake,.—
To go up, mount, ascend: a pedibusque minutatim succedere frigus Non dubitabat,: ad summum honorem,: ille ad superos Succedet famā,: aurum in summum successit honorem,.—
To approach, draw near (class. and freq.).
Milit. t. t., to march on, advance, march up to, approach (class. and freq.; cf.: invado, progredior):

sub primam nostram aciem successerunt, : sub montem,: supra hostium munitionem, Sisenn. ap. : ad castra hostium infestis signis,: ad stationes hostium,: ad hostium latebras,: ad urbem,: ad moenia,: sub ipsum vallum,: ad portūs claustra,: celeriter ad molem,: moenibus,; : munimentis,: munitionibus, Auct. B. Alex. 30, 4: portas succedunt,: murum,.—Absol.: classis paulatim successit,.—Impers. pass.: ubicumque iniquo successum est loco,.—

To follow, follow after, take the place of, relieve, come into the place of, succeed; to succeed to, receive by succession (syn. subsequor).
Lit.: ut integri et recentes defatigatis succederent,; ; ; cf. ; : in stationem,: in pugnam,; for which, proelio,: in paternas opes,: in Pompeii locum heres,; cf.: Sequani principatum dimiserant. In eorum locum Remi successerant,: ego in ejus quem occidissem succederem locum,: succedam ego vicarius tuo muneri,; ; ; cf. ; : qui regno successit,: post ejus mortem frater regno successit,: in hujus locum filia regno successit,; but: in regnum,: huic Mithridates filius succedit,: ad alteram partem succedunt Ubii,follow, come next,.—Of things: aspicit in teretes lignum succedere suras,. — Impers. pass.: non solum, quod tibi succederetur, sed quod Gabinio non succederetur,: te antea, quam tibi successum esset, decessurum fuisse,.—
Trop.
To come or enter into a relation: in affinitatis jura,.—
To follow, follow after, succeed.
In time: successit ipse magnis (oratoribus),: horum aetati successit Isocrates,; cf.: nihil semper floret: aetas succedit aetati,: tertia post illas successit aënea proles,: quorum priores duae probationi succedunt,: in Italiā violis succedit rosa,: etenim ei succedo orationi, quae, etc., I succeed, I speak after an oration, which, etc., : consules, quo majori gloriae rerum gestarum succedere se cernebant,: rex ... succedens tantae caritati Hieronis,: ut bono succedenti regi difficilis aemulatio esset,.—
To follow, take the place of, succeed in value: cujus (purpurae) libra denariis centum venibat ... huic successit dibapha Tyria, quae in libras denariis mille non poterat emi, Nep. ap. : in vicem ejus (graminis) succedit decoctum,: non numero tantum amissorum civium, sed et dignitati,: filii magnitudini patris successerunt,.—Pass. impers.: male gestis rebus alterius successum est,.—
Hence, to follow the nature or rule of any thing, to belong to a class or category (rare): succedere hanc quoque comparativo generi,: quae omnia succedunt legitimis quaestionibus,.—
Pregn.: res (alicui) succedit, or simply succedit, goes on well, is successful, prospers, succeeds (cf. evenit): lepide hoc succedit sub manus negotium,: negotium (ei) sub manus,; : quando hoc bene successit,: parum succedit, quod ago,: pleraque non succedunt,: quod res nulla successerat,: inceptum non succedebat,: nihil conceptae temere spei succedebat,: voti Phoebus succedere partem Mente dedit,: si prospere prima successerint,.—Absol.: hac non successit: aliā ingrediemur viā,: si quando minus succedet,: si ex sententiā successerit,: si proinde, ut ipse mereor, mihi successerit, Planc. ap. : si successisset coeptis,: inceptis,: fraudi,, 25: facinori eorum, et saep.: successurumque Minervae Indoluit,.—Pass.: cum omnia meā causā velles mihi successa, Cic. Fil. ap. .—Impers.: nolle successum non patribus,: ubicumque iniquo successum erat loco, Weissenb. ad loc.

a follower, successor in office, possession, time, etc. (class.; cf. vicarius): conjunctissimus,; cf.: successori decessor invidit,; ; ; : successorem alicui mittere,to remove from office,; cf. : legato eum consulari successorem dedisse,; : successorem accipere,to be removed,: successores Alexandri,: studii successor et heres,: quo successore (Philoctete) sagittae Herculis utuntur,i. e. the succeeding possessor, inheritor,: alieni criminis successor,: successore novo vincitur omnis amor,by a new favorite,; cf.: novus habendus (clipeo),: propositi successor honoris Junius,: successor fuit hic tibi, Galle; Propertius illi,i. e. he followed you, wrote after you,.—Of a female: Phoebe, Fraternis successor equis, Corn. succinctus, a, um,
Part. and P. a. of succingo.

la:noun:successus.html:
successus, ūs, m.
succedo
.
(Acc. to succedo, I.) An advance, approach (very rare).
Lit.: successus et incursus hostium,: equorum,.—
Transf. (post-class.), a place which one goes down into, a cavern: terrarum,; .—
(Acc. to succedo, II.) A succession of time, continuance (post-class.): continuo totius temporis successu,: ex successu continuae felicitatis obliviscitur se hominem,.—
Trop., a happy issue, good result, success (the usual signif.; perh. not ante-Aug.): successu exsultans,: Mnestheus successu acrior ipso,: hos successus alit,: successum dea dira negat,; cf.: multo successu Fabiis audaciam crescere,: contentus fortuito successu,: elatus successu, § 3: successumque artes non habuere meae, Ov. R.

Am. 624: successu rerum ferocior,; ; ; : successus improborum plures allicit,; ; ; : petitionum,: artis,: nec successum victoriae moderatus est,: tantusque rerum successu haberi coeptus est,: successu rerum florentes opes,; .— Plur.: pleni successibus anni,: successus prosperos dare, Liv. prooem. § 13: ne successibus deesset auctoritas,.—

Concr., posterity, issue (post-class.): ferunt Graecorum commenta ... feminam ... suā manu suos exstinxisse successus, i. e. Medea,.

la:verb:succingo.gloss: to gather or tuck up (with a belt, etc.)
senses: to gather or tuck up (with a belt, etc.)
la:verb:succingo.html:
suc-cingo (subc-), nxi, nctum, 3, v. a.,
to gird below or from below, to tuck up, gird, gird about, girdle (mostly poet. and in postAug. prose; cf. subligo).
Lit.: crure tenus medio tunicas,: astricti succingant ilia ventres,; cf.: Virginem et Leonem Anguis intortus succingit, (7), 1: illa (Scylla) feris atram canibus succingitur alvum,; cf. ; : eāpse sic succincta,tucked up,: amicus,: popa,cursor,: anus,: Diana,; cf.: vestem ritu succincta Dianae,; 9, 89.— Poet.: succincta comas pinus,with its bare trunk,; : quis illaec est, quae lugubri Succincta est stolā, girt about, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 134 Vahl.): succincti gladiis mediā regione cracentes, girt about, armed, id. ap. Fest. s. v. cracentes, p. 53 (Ann. v. 497 ib.): gladio succinctus,: succinctam pharetrā,: pallā succincta cruenta,; cf. amictu,: succincti corda machaeris, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 392 ib.): pugione succinctus, Anton. ap. : cultro succinctus,: ferro,; .—
Transf., to surround, furnish, provide, equip, fit out with any thing (syn.: saepio, circumdo): quod multo se pluribus et majoribus canibus succinxerat,: frustra se terrore succinxerit,: his animum succinge bonis,: succinctam latrantibus inguina monstris,: Scylla rapax canibus succincta Molossis,: virgineam canibus succincta figuram,: Carthago succincta portubus,: succinctus armis legionibusque,: maximarum gentium viribus,: totius ferme Orientis viribus,: horum scientiā debet esse succinctus,: patriā papyro,.—Hence, succinctus, a, um, P. a. (very rare and post-Aug.).
Prepared, ready for any thing: proni atque succincti ad omnem clausulam,.—
Contracted, short, concise, succinct (poet. and post-Aug.; cf.: brevis, circumscriptus): libelli,: arbores succinctiores,: succinctior brevitas,med.—Adv.: suc-cinctē, briefly, concisely, succinctly (late Lat.; cf.: breviter, strictim): docere,.—Comp.: fari,: dimicare,.

suc-cendo, di, sum, 3, v. a.

Quadrig. ap. ; : rogum,: pontem,: pinus duabus manibus,: urbem suis manibus,: aër fulminibus succenditur,; : aras,.—
Transf., to inflame, redden: illi rubor igneus ora Succendit,: purpura infecit niveos vultus per liquidas succensa genas,.—
Trop., to kindle, inflame with passion, etc. (only poet.; cf. succenseo): succendit Castora Phoebe,: Deucalion Pyrrhae succensus amore,: altera succensa cupidine,: patriā succensa senectā (i. e. amore patris senis), (4, 18), 15: (furorem) succendunt classica cantu,; cf.: in bella succensi mero,: succensas agit libido mentes,: succensi irā,: luctu succensus,: dulcedine famae succensus,: mens facibus pudoris,.

la:noun:sucus.html:
sūcus (succus), i (collat. form,
gen. sing. sucūs, ; gen. plur. sucuum, ), m.
sugo
, juice, moisture, sap (class.; cf.: liquor, latex).
Lit.
In gen.: stirpes ex terrā sucum trahunt,: sucus ex intestinis et alvo secretus a reliquo cibo,: cochleae suo sibi suco vivunt,: ambrosiae suco saturi (equi solis),; so, ambrosiae,: uvae,; : sucus nuci expressus, et saep.: corpus suci plenum,i. e. plump,: facies suci palaestrici plena,.—Of other liquids: garo (mixtum) de sucis piscis Hiberi,: corpora suco pinguis olivi Splendescunt,oil,: aluntur bubuli lactis suco,: inbui lactis sucos,: ratio faciendi (unguenti) duplex, sucus et corpus: ille olei generibus fere constat, hoc odorum,: vini,, praef. 2, § 2: candidus ovi,. —
In partic., a medicinal liquor, a drink, draught, potion (poet.): purgantes pectora suci,; ; ; ; ; ; .—
Transf., the taste of any thing, flavor: sucum sentimus in ore, cibum cum Mandendo exprimimus, (cf. χυμός): ova suci melioris,: Picenis cedunt pomis Tiburtia suco,: celantia sucum,: cantharus ingratus suco,.—
Trop., strength, rigor, energy, spirit: sucus ac sanguis (civitatis),: ingenii, Quint. prooem. § 24. —
Esp., of the vigor of

a discourse, spirit, life: ornatur oratio ... suco suo,: sucus ille et sanguis incorruptus usque ad hanc aetatem oratorum fuit,: orationis subtilitas etsi non plurimi sanguinis est, habeat tamen sucum aliquem oportet,: omnes etiam tum retinebant illum Pericli sucum,: historia quoque alere orationem quodam uberi jucundoque suco potest,.

Part. fut. pass.: peccata hominum non succensenda sunt,.
